literature.headline_zh: 人偏肺病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: XGBoost和逻辑回归模型表现出相当的性能,XGBoost在训练集和测试集上的AUC分别为0.87(95% CI:0.84–0.90)和0.78(95% CI:0.72–0.85)。SHAP分析确定喘息、年龄和肺部啰音是最具影响力的预测因子。 [10.1186/s12890-026-04816-9]

最常见的临床表现和症状包括咳嗽(64例;82.1%)、发热(59例;75.6%)以及呼吸窘迫迹象,包括呼吸急促(48例;61.5%)和肋间凹陷(38例;48.7%)。食欲减退(32例;41%)和流涕(29例;37.2%)也较为常见。41例(52.6%)患者进行了胸部X光检查,所有病例均显示异常结果,最常见的异常为肺实变。25.6%的患者检测到病毒合并感染,24.4%检测到细菌病原体。 [10.1186/s13052-026-02364-w]
RSV和HBoV在婴儿和幼儿中最为常见,这与气道和免疫系统发育一致(Feng等,2024;Jiang等,2016;Li等,2022);ADV在学龄儿童中达到高峰,IFV在较大的学龄前至学龄儿童群体中达到高峰,这与学校及其他拥挤环境中的密切接触有关(Fang等,2025;Yu等,2021;Zhang等,2023);而HMPV则表现出中间分布。 [PMCID:PMC13645514]
人偏肺病毒 主要针对呼吸道上皮,触发 免疫应答,从而有助于病毒清除和疾病 发病机制。包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂在内的研究疗法显示出希望,但需要进一步验证。免疫调节剂和草药可能会提供支持性益处,但它们对抗 HMPV 的功效尚未得到证实。疫苗 的开发正在进行中,有几个候选药物处于临床前和早期临床阶段。 [10.2174/0122113525396349251011213223]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: XGBoost and logistic regression models demonstrated comparable performance, with XGBoost achieving an AUC of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.84–0.90) and 0.78 (95% CI: 0.72–0.85) on the training and testing sets, respectively. SHAP analysis identified wheezing, age, and pulmonary rales as the most influential predictors. [10.1186/s12890-026-04816-9]

The most frequent signs and symptoms were cough (64;82.1%), fever (59;75.6%), and signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea (48;61.5%) and subcostal retraction (38;48.7%). Hyporexia (32;41%) and coryza (29;37.2%) were also common. [10.1186/s13052-026-02364-w]

RSV and HBoV were most prevalent in infants and toddlers, in line with airway and immune development (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Li et al., 2022); ADV peaked in school-aged children and IFV in the older preschool-to-school-age range, consistent with close-contact transmission in schools and other crowded settings (Fang et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023); and HMPV showed an intermediate distribution. [PMCID:PMC13645514]

Human metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. [10.2174/0122113525396349251011213223]

brief_items_zh: 本期人偏肺病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
XGBoost和逻辑回归模型表现出相当的性能,XGBoost在训练集和测试集上的AUC分别为0.87(95% CI:0.84–0.90)和0.78(95% CI:0.72–0.85)。SHAP分析确定喘息、年龄和肺部啰音是最具影响力的预测因子。
最常见的临床表现和症状包括咳嗽(64例;82.1%)、发热(59例;75.6%)以及呼吸窘迫迹象,包括呼吸急促(48例;61.5%)和肋间凹陷(38例;48.7%)。食欲减退(32例;41%)和流涕(29例;37.2%)也较为常见。41例(52.6%)患者进行了胸部X光检查,所有病例均显示异常结果,最常见的异常为肺实变。25.6%的患者检测到病毒合并感染,24.4%检测到细菌病原体。
RSV和HBoV在婴儿和幼儿中最为常见,这与气道和免疫系统发育一致(Feng等,2024;Jiang等,2016;Li等,2022);ADV在学龄儿童中达到高峰,IFV在较大的学龄前至学龄儿童群体中达到高峰,这与学校及其他拥挤环境中的密切接触有关(Fang等,2025;Yu等,2021;Zhang等,2023);而HMPV则表现出中间分布。
人偏肺病毒 主要针对呼吸道上皮,触发 免疫应答,从而有助于病毒清除和疾病 发病机制。包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂在内的研究疗法显示出希望,但需要进一步验证。免疫调节剂和草药可能会提供支持性益处,但它们对抗 HMPV 的功效尚未得到证实。疫苗 的开发正在进行中,有几个候选药物处于临床前和早期临床阶段。

papers.title: Human metapneumovirus infection in hospitalized children: a four-year retrospective study from a tertiary pediatric hospital
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important viral cause of acute respiratory infections, particularly in young children, and may lead to hospitalization for lower respiratory tract disease. However, detailed clinical data from hospitalized pediatric cohorts remain limited. This study combined two complementary datasets from a tertiary pediatric hospital in Palermo, Italy. The hospital microbiology dataset included all PCR-confirmed hMPV detections recorded from October 2021 to May 2025 ( n = 636, including 560 pediatric cases) and was used only to describe temporal distribution. The clinical cohort comprised 78 of the pediatric cases who were hospitalized in the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Unit between January 2022 and May 2025 and had complete clinical records. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological, and therapeutic data were collected and analyzed through IBM SPSS Statistics using descriptive statistics and exploratory bivariate analyses. Continuous variables were summarized as median and interquartile range (IQR), while categorical variables were reported as absolute frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between children who received antibiotics and those who did not were performed using Pearson’s chi-square or exact tests, as appropriate. Associations between categorical predictors and length of hospital stay were explored using the Mann–Whitney U test. Correlation with age was assessed using Spearman’s coefficient. The median age of hospitalized children was 14 months (IQR 3–30). The most frequent signs and symptoms were cough (64;82.1%), fever (59;75.6%), and signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea (48;61.5%) and subcostal retraction (38;48.7%). Hyporexia (32;41%) and coryza (29;37.2%) were also common. Chest X-ray was performed in 41 (52.6%) patients and showed abnormal findings in all cases, most commonly consolidation patterns. Viral coinfections were detected in 25.6% of patients, and bacterial organisms were detected in 24.4%. Oxygen support was required in 60.3% of cases, and five patients (6.4%) required pediatric intensive care admission. Antibiotics were prescribed in 70.5% of patients, although bacterial organisms were detected in only 24.4%. Our findings describe the clinical characteristics and management of hospitalized children with hMPV infection in a tertiary pediatric center, highlighting the clinical relevance of hMPV among hospitalized children in our center. Moreover, the high rate of antibiotic prescription observed in this cohort highlights the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing viral from bacterial respiratory infections and underscores the importance of improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important viral cause of acute respiratory infections, particularly in young children, and may lead to hospitalization for lower respiratory tract disease. However, detailed clinical data from hospitalized pediatric cohorts remain limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study combined two complementary datasets from a tertiary pediatric hospital in Palermo, Italy. The clinical cohort comprised 78 of the pediatric cases who were hospitalized in the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Unit between January 2022 and May 2025 and had complete clinical records.
analysis.methods: Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological, and therapeutic data were collected and analyzed through IBM SPSS Statistics using descriptive statistics and exploratory bivariate analyses. Continuous variables were summarized as median and interquartile range (IQR), while categorical variables were reported as absolute frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between children who received antibiotics and those who did not were performed using Pearson’s chi-square or exact tests, as appropriate.
analysis.main_results: The most frequent signs and symptoms were cough (64;82.1%), fever (59;75.6%), and signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea (48;61.5%) and subcostal retraction (38;48.7%). Hyporexia (32;41%) and coryza (29;37.2%) were also common. Chest X-ray was performed in 41 (52.6%) patients and showed abnormal findings in all cases, most commonly consolidation patterns. Viral coinfections were detected in 25.6% of patients, and bacterial organisms were detected in 24.4%.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings describe the clinical characteristics and management of hospitalized children with hMPV infection in a tertiary pediatric center, highlighting the clinical relevance of hMPV among hospitalized children in our center. Moreover, the high rate of antibiotic prescription observed in this cohort highlights the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing viral from bacterial respiratory infections and underscores the importance of improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can cautiously inform improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease, emphasizing the need for better diagnostic tools to differentiate viral from bacterial infections in hospitalized children.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, as it included only 78 hospitalized pediatric cases with complete clinical records. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the focus on a single tertiary pediatric center.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the clinical characteristics and management of hospitalized children with human metapneumovirus (hMPV) infection in a tertiary pediatric hospital in Palermo, Italy, over a four-year period. The research highlights the importance of hMPV as a cause of acute respiratory infections in young children, particularly those requiring hospitalization. The study combined two datasets, one describing the temporal distribution of hMPV infections and the other focusing on clinical data from 78 hospitalized cases. Key findings include the high prevalence of symptoms such as cough, fever, and respiratory distress, as well as the frequent use of antibiotics despite limited bacterial coinfections. The study underscores the diagnostic challenges in differentiating viral from bacterial respiratory infections and calls for improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance. However, the study is limited by its retrospective design and potential selection bias, as it included only a subset of cases with complete records, which may affect the generalizability of the findings.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important viral cause of acute respiratory infections, particularly in young children, and may lead to hospitalization for lower respiratory tract disease. However, detailed clinical data from hospitalized pediatric cohorts remain limited.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: This study combined two complementary datasets from a tertiary pediatric hospital in Palermo, Italy. The clinical cohort comprised 78 of the pediatric cases who were hospitalized in the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Unit between January 2022 and May 2025 and had complete clinical records.
elements_en.methods: Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological, and therapeutic data were collected and analyzed through IBM SPSS Statistics using descriptive statistics and exploratory bivariate analyses. Continuous variables were summarized as median and interquartile range (IQR), while categorical variables were reported as absolute frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between children who received antibiotics and those who did not were performed using Pearson’s chi-square or exact tests, as appropriate.
elements_en.main_results: The most frequent signs and symptoms were cough (64;82.1%), fever (59;75.6%), and signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea (48;61.5%) and subcostal retraction (38;48.7%). Hyporexia (32;41%) and coryza (29;37.2%) were also common. Chest X-ray was performed in 41 (52.6%) patients and showed abnormal findings in all cases, most commonly consolidation patterns. Viral coinfections were detected in 25.6% of patients, and bacterial organisms were detected in 24.4%.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Our findings describe the clinical characteristics and management of hospitalized children with hMPV infection in a tertiary pediatric center, highlighting the clinical relevance of hMPV among hospitalized children in our center. Moreover, the high rate of antibiotic prescription observed in this cohort highlights the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing viral from bacterial respiratory infections and underscores the importance of improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can cautiously inform improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease, emphasizing the need for better diagnostic tools to differentiate viral from bacterial infections in hospitalized children.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and potential for selection bias, as it included only 78 hospitalized pediatric cases with complete clinical records. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited sample size and the focus on a single tertiary pediatric center.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人偏肺病毒(hMPV)是急性呼吸道感染的重要病原体,尤其是在婴幼儿中,可能导致下呼吸道疾病住院。然而,关于住院儿科患者人偏肺病毒感染的详细临床数据仍然有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究结合了意大利巴勒莫一家三级儿科医院的两个互补数据集。临床数据集包括2022年1月至2025年5月期间在儿科感染性疾病病房住院的78例儿科病例,这些病例具有完整的临床记录。
elements_zh.methods: 通过IBM SPSS Statistics收集和分析了人口学、临床、实验室、影像学和治疗数据,采用描述性统计和探索性双变量分析。连续变量以中位数和四分位数范围(IQR)进行总结,而分类变量则以绝对频数和百分比进行报告。使用Pearson卡方检验或精确检验(根据情况)比较接受抗生素治疗和未接受抗生素治疗的儿童。
elements_zh.main_results: 最常见的临床表现和症状包括咳嗽(64例;82.1%)、发热(59例;75.6%)以及呼吸窘迫迹象,包括呼吸急促(48例;61.5%)和肋间凹陷(38例;48.7%)。食欲减退(32例;41%)和流涕(29例;37.2%)也较为常见。41例(52.6%)患者进行了胸部X光检查,所有病例均显示异常结果,最常见的异常为肺实变。25.6%的患者检测到病毒合并感染,24.4%检测到细菌病原体。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 我们的研究结果描述了在三级儿科中心住院的人偏肺病毒感染儿童的临床特征和管理情况,突显了人偏肺病毒在我们中心住院儿童中的临床重要性。此外,本研究中观察到的高抗生素处方率突显了在区分病毒性与细菌性呼吸道感染方面的诊断挑战,并强调了在儿科呼吸道疾病中改善抗菌药物使用和病毒学监测的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以谨慎地用于改善儿科呼吸道疾病中的抗菌药物使用和病毒学监测,强调了需要更好的诊断工具来区分病毒性与细菌性感染在住院儿童中的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其回顾性设计和可能的选择偏倚,因为仅包括了78例具有完整临床记录的住院儿科病例。由于样本量有限以及仅关注单一三级儿科中心,证据强度中等。

papers.title_zh: 人偏肺病毒感染住院儿童:意大利巴勒莫一家三级儿科医院四年的回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is an important viral cause of acute respiratory infections, particularly in young children, and may lead to hospitalization for lower respiratory tract disease. However, detailed clinical data from hospitalized pediatric cohorts remain limited. This study combined two complementary datasets from a tertiary pediatric hospital in Palermo, Italy. The hospital microbiology dataset included all PCR-confirmed hMPV detections recorded from October 2021 to May 2025 ( n = 636, including 560 pediatric cases) and was used only to describe temporal distribution. The clinical cohort comprised 78 of the pediatric cases who were hospitalized in the Pediatric Infectious Diseases Unit between January 2022 and May 2025 and had complete clinical records. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, radiological, and therapeutic data were collected and analyzed through IBM SPSS Statistics using descriptive statistics and exploratory bivariate analyses. Continuous variables were summarized as median and interquartile range (IQR), while categorical variables were reported as absolute frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between children who received antibiotics and those who did not were performed using Pearson’s chi-square or exact tests, as appropriate. Associations between categorical predictors and length of hospital stay were explored using the Mann–Whitney U test. Correlation with age was assessed using Spearman’s coefficient. The median age of hospitalized children was 14 months (IQR 3–30). The most frequent signs and symptoms were cough (64;82.1%), fever (59;75.6%), and signs of respiratory distress, including tachypnea (48;61.5%) and subcostal retraction (38;48.7%). Hyporexia (32;41%) and coryza (29;37.2%) were also common. Chest X-ray was performed in 41 (52.6%) patients and showed abnormal findings in all cases, most commonly consolidation patterns. Viral coinfections were detected in 25.6% of patients, and bacterial organisms were detected in 24.4%. Oxygen support was required in 60.3% of cases, and five patients (6.4%) required pediatric intensive care admission. Antibiotics were prescribed in 70.5% of patients, although bacterial organisms were detected in only 24.4%. Our findings describe the clinical characteristics and management of hospitalized children with hMPV infection in a tertiary pediatric center, highlighting the clinical relevance of hMPV among hospitalized children in our center. Moreover, the high rate of antibiotic prescription observed in this cohort highlights the diagnostic challenges in distinguishing viral from bacterial respiratory infections and underscores the importance of improved antimicrobial stewardship and virological surveillance in pediatric respiratory disease.

papers.title: Emerging Trends in the Pathogenesis, Diagnosis, and Management of Human Metapneumovirus-Associated Respiratory Infections
papers.abstract: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the pathogenesis, diagnosis, and management of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) infections, emphasizing its impact on vulnerable populations. The evidence highlights the virus's targeting of respiratory epithelium and the immune responses it triggers. While investigational therapies like fusion and protease inhibitors show promise, their efficacy remains unproven. Vaccine development is ongoing, with several candidates in early stages. The review underscores the need for further clinical trials, improved diagnostics, and public awareness to address the public health burden of HMPV. Despite the lack of specific treatments and vaccines, the study suggests that emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 人偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 感染和疾病。该综述重点关注 发病机制、诊断 和 HMPV 相关呼吸道感染的管理,特别是幼儿、免疫功能低下者和老年人等弱势群体。

papers.source_body_en: Introduction: Human Metapneumovirus is a significant respiratory pathogen causing infections across all age groups, particularly in young children, immunocompromised individuals, and the elderly. Despite its clinical relevance, there are currently no approved vaccines or specific antiviral treatments for Human Metapneumovirus, necessitating further research into therapeutic and preventive strategies. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed journals, clinical trials, and recent studies focusing on Human Metapneumovirus infection. Data were extracted and analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of antiviral therapies, monoclonal antibodies, immunomodulators, and vaccine candidates. Results: Studies indicate that Human Metapneumovirus primarily targets the respiratory epithelium, triggering immune responses that contribute to both viral clearance and disease pathogenesis. Investigational therapies, including fusion inhibitors and protease inhibitors, show promise but require further validation. Immunomodulatory agents and herbal remedies may offer supportive benefits, but their efficacy against Human Metapneumovirus remains unproven. Advances in vaccine development are ongoing, with several candidates in preclinical and early clinical stages. Discussion: HMPV continues to pose a substantial public health burden due to its seasonal outbreaks, clinical similarity to other respiratory viruses, and absence of specific therapies. The virus evades immune responses via multiple mechanisms, contributing to disease severity, particularly in vulnerable populations. Although supportive care is currently the mainstay, emerging antivirals and vaccines may offer future solutions. Improved diagnostic access, public awareness, and targeted research are essential for controlling HMPV infections. Conclusion: Human Metapneumovirus continues to pose a public health challenge due to the lack of targeted treatments and vaccines. Ongoing research into antiviral agents, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines is critical for effective disease management. Further clinical trials are needed to establish safe and effective therapeutic options.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言:人偏肺病毒(HMPV)是一种重要的呼吸道病原体,可在不同年龄段人群中引发感染,尤其是在幼儿、免疫功能低下者及老年人中。尽管其具有重要的临床意义,但目前尚无获批的抗病毒药物或针对人偏肺病毒的特异性治疗方法,亟需进一步研究治疗和预防策略。方法:通过系统性文献综述,检索同行评议期刊、临床试验及近期研究,重点关注人偏肺病毒感染。提取并分析数据,以评估抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体、免疫调节剂及疫苗候选物的有效性。结果:研究表明,人偏肺病毒主要靶向呼吸道上皮细胞,触发免疫应答,这些免疫应答既有助于病毒清除,也会导致疾病发病机制。正在研发的治疗方法,包括融合抑制剂和蛋白酶抑制剂,显示出潜力,但仍需进一步验证。免疫调节剂和中草药可能提供支持性益处,但其对人偏肺病毒的有效性尚未得到证实。疫苗研发取得进展,多个候选疫苗已进入临床前及早期临床阶段。讨论:由于人偏肺病毒的季节性流行、与其他呼吸道病毒的临床相似性以及缺乏特异性治疗方法,该病毒继续对公共卫生构成重大负担。该病毒通过多种机制逃避免疫应答,导致疾病严重程度增加,尤其是在易感人群中。尽管目前主要采用支持性治疗,但新兴的抗病毒药物和疫苗可能为未来提供解决方案。改善诊断可及性、提高公众意识及开展针对性研究对于控制人偏肺病毒感染至关重要。结论:由于缺乏针对性治疗方法和疫苗,人偏肺病毒继续对公共卫生构成挑战。针对抗病毒药物、单克隆抗体及疫苗的持续研究对于有效疾病管理至关重要。亟需进一步临床试验以确立安全有效的治疗方案。

papers.full_text: Abstract Objective To develop and validate a machine learning–based model to accurately classify the risk of severe pneumonia in children infected with hMPV. Methods This retrospective cohort study consecutively enrolled clinical data from 854 hospitalized children with hMPV-associated pneumonia at Kunming Children’s Hospital between December 2019 and March 2025. According to guideline-based criteria, patients were classified into a severe pneumonia group (n = 203) and a non-severe pneumonia group (n = 651). The dataset was randomly divided into a training set and a testing set at a 7:3 ratio. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression. Six machine learning models, including logistic regression, k-nearest neighbors, naïve Bayes, multilayer perceptron, random forest, and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), were constructed and compared in the training set. Model performance in the independent testing set was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and F1 score. Clinical net benefit was assessed using decision curve analysis, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were applied to visually interpret the optimal model. Results LASSO regression identified 9 core predictors: age, wheezing, pulmonary rales, pleural effusion, ferritin, lactate dehydrogenase, neutrophil percentage, neutrophil count, and albumin. Among the six models, XGBoost and logistic regression demonstrated comparable overall performance. XGBoost achieved a training set AUC of 0.87 (95% CI: 0.84–0.90) and a test set AUC of 0.78 (95% CI: 0.72–0.85). The accuracy on the training set was 0.81, the sensitivity was 0.99, the specificity was 0.23, and the F1 score was 0.89; the accuracy on the test set was 0.79, the sensitivity was 0.98, the specificity was 0.17, and the F1 score was 0.88.Decision curve analysis indicated that the model provided a favorable clinical net benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis revealed that wheezing, age, and pulmonary rales were the three most influential predictors. Conclusion We successfully developed and validated machine learning models, particularly XGBoost and logistic regression, for risk classification of severe pneumonia in children with hMPV infection. The model demonstrated strong discriminative performance, clinical utility, and interpretability, and may serve as a valuable decision-support tool for risk stratification of high-risk pediatric patients. papers.abstract_zh: 方法 本项回顾性队列研究研究连续纳入了2019年12月至2025年3月期间昆明儿童医院收治的854例与人偏肺病毒(hMPV)相关的肺炎患儿的临床数据。结果 基于LASSO回归,确定了9个核心预测因子:年龄、喘息、肺部湿啰音、胸腔积液、铁蛋白、乳酸脱氢酶、中性粒细胞百分比、中性粒细胞计数和白蛋白。结论 我们成功开发并验证了基于机器学习的模型,特别是XGBoost和逻辑回归模型,用于对hMPV感染儿童严重肺炎风险进行分类。伦理声明 伦理批准和参与同意 本研究已获得昆明医科大学儿童医院伦理审查委员会的批准。由于本研究为回顾性设计,昆明医科大学儿童医院伦理审查委员会(KMSETYY-IIT-2025-002(GC))豁免了知情同意的要求。此外,所有方法均按照相关指南和法规或赫尔辛基宣言进行。摘要 目的 开发并验证一个基于机器学习的模型,以准确分类hMPV感染儿童严重肺炎的风险。根据基于指南的标准,患者被分为严重肺炎组(n = 203)和非严重肺炎组(n = 651)。数据集以7:3的比例随机分为训练集和测试集。使用最小绝对收缩和选择算子(LASSO)回归进行特征选择。包括逻辑回归、k近邻、朴素贝叶斯、多层感知机、随机森林和极端梯度提升在内的六种机器学习模型被用于分析。

papers.full_text: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%). Age distributions differed by pathogen (p<0.05): RSV and HBoV predominated in infants and toddlers, HRV and HMPV in preschoolers, ADV in school-aged children, and IFV across the older preschool-to-school-age range; males predominated for all viruses except IFV. Five viruses peaked in December, whereas HBoV peaked uniquely in July. After adjustment for seasonality and secular trend, the unadjusted associations of IFV with humidity and temperature disappeared, indicating that they largely reflected shared seasonality. In contrast, RSV retained associations with temperature (RR 3.87, 95% CI 1.39–10.76) and wind speed (RR 5.46, 95% CI 2.39–12.47) at a 1-month lag, and HMPV with temperature (RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.64–108.3; imprecise given its low case count); HRV, ADV, and HBoV showed no independent climatic associations. Co-infections occurred in 116 cases (4.5%), most frequently HBoV+HRV (23.3%).ConclusionPost-pandemic pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin shows distinctive pathogen-specific profiles in age, seasonality, and climatic sensitivity. The summer peak of HBoV and the seasonally independent climatic drivers of RSV and HMPV provide a preliminary basis that, if confirmed with higher-resolution data, could inform pathogen-tailored, climate-informed surveillance in northern Chinese megacities. 2Materials and methods2.1Study design, setting and populationWe conducted a retrospective single-center surveillance study at the Department of Respiratory Medicine, Tianjin Children’s Hospital (Ma-Chang campus), the only tertiary-A comprehensive children’s hospital in Tianjin. The hospital is the principal pediatric referral center for Tianjin municipality and, for selected specialties, draws patients from across the wider North China Plain; publicly reported hospital-wide figures indicate roughly 17,000–20,000 pediatric admissions per year across all departments. Our cohort of 2,597 virologically confirmed viral LRTI cases represents the subset of hospitalized LRTI cases that were both tested and found positive for one of the six target viruses, not the total burden of pediatric LRTI hospitalization in Tianjin. A precise, denominator-based estimate of the proportion of all Tianjin pediatric LRTI hospitalizations captured by this cohort is not available, because no citywide pediatric LRTI hospitalization registry exists for comparison. As a tertiary referral center, the cohort is likely enriched for more severe disease and for cases referred from primary and secondary facilities; this referral pattern, and the resulting limit on generalizability to primary care, is revisited in the Discussion (Section 4.6).Eligible participants were children aged 0–18 years hospitalized with a clinical diagnosis of LRTI between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2025, from whom a respiratory specimen was submitted for routine viral testing. LRTI was defined clinically, following the 2019 Chinese Pediatric Society guideline for community-acquired pneumonia (Subspecialty Group of Respiratory Diseases, 2019), as cough or fever (axillary temperature ≥38 °C) together with at least one of: tachypnoea, wheezing, crackles on auscultation, or imaging evidence of pneumonia or bronchiolitis. This definition captures the clinical syndromes of pneumonia and bronchiolitis and excludes isolated upper respiratory tract infection. We excluded children with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease, congenital airway malformations, documented immunodeficiency, active malignancy, or concurrent infection by pathogens outside the predefined six-virus panel. This last criterion operated at the level of the child rather than of the laboratory result: whenever the tNGS report carried a Class A detection of a bacterial, atypical or non-panel viral pathogen alongside one of the six target viruses, the case was removed from the cohort at eligibility screening, so no such child contributes to any analysis reported here. For viruses prone to subclinical carriage, chiefly HRV and HBoV, a detection was considered clinically causative only when the tNGS reporting algorithm assigned a pathogenicity Class A grade, the clinical picture matched the corresponding viral syndrome, and other plausible infectious causes had been clinically excluded (residual misclassification risk for these two viruses is discussed in Section 4.6). For descriptive analyses, children were stratified a priori into four age categories: infants (<1 year), toddlers (1–2 years), preschoolers (3–5 years) and school-aged children (≥6 years). All records were de-identified before analysis. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Tianjin Children’s Hospital (approval number 2024-LXKY-023); written informed consent was waived given the retrospective design and full de-identification of the dataset.2.2Pathogen detectionRespiratory specimens (sputum, the predominant type; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF; nasopharyngeal swabs; and oropharyngeal swabs) were collected following standardized clinical protocols, placed into viral transport medium, and transported within two hours at 2–8 °C to the clinical laboratory. Total nucleic acids were extracted on an automated platform following the manufacturer’s instructions. All specimens were tested with the same commercial targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) panel, which simultaneously screens for respiratory bacteria, viruses, atypical pathogens and antimicrobial-resistance markers. Library construction, ultra-multiplex amplification of pathogen-specific genomic regions and Illumina-compatible high-throughput sequencing were performed following the manufacturer’s recommended workflow, with reads aligned against a curated pathogen reference database (Li et al., 2025; Shang et al., 2025). The vendor’s reporting algorithm assigned each detected organism a clinical pathogenicity grade, from Class A (highest confidence) through lower-confidence grades. The panel was introduced during 2023 and reached full clinical implementation in the fourth quarter of that year, after which testing volume remained broadly stable through 2024 and 2025. Monthly counts of tNGS requests could not be retrieved from the laboratory information system for the whole study window, so this account of testing volume rests on the laboratory’s implementation record rather than on an auditable series of test counts, and it should be read as such.The grade is a composite call rather than a single read-count cut-off. It is generated by an integrated scoring system that combines normalized read counts (reads per million, RPM), the breadth of genome coverage achieved across the targeted regions, and species-level annotation of pathogenicity against a curated reference database; Class A is assigned to organisms that meet the pre-specified RPM and coverage criteria for a clinically significant pathogen. The numerical RPM and coverage cut-offs behind the grade are proprietary to the assay vendor and are not released to the ordering laboratory; we are therefore unable to report them, and the grade as issued was the only form in which this information was available to us. Grading was prospective in the sense that it was performed by the clinical laboratory at the time the routine diagnostic report was issued and used for patient care, and the research team did not re-adjudicate the classifications retrospectively. No Class A detection was subsequently excluded on the grounds of clinical mismatch, because the Class A flag served as an inclusion criterion for the six-virus panel rather than as the sole determinant of clinical causality; for HRV and HBoV, the additional clinical adjudication described in Section 2.1 was applied instead.The full panel detects a broader range of organisms than the six viruses analyzed here. Common bacterial pathogens reported by the full panel include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus; the atypical pathogens include Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia pneumoniae; and respiratory viruses outside the six-virus panel, including parainfluenza viruses, seasonal coronaviruses and SARS-CoV-2, are likewise covered. Consistent with the eligibility criteria set out in Section 2.1, a child in whom any of these organisms was reported concurrently with one of the six target viruses was excluded from the cohort at screening rather than merely omitted from the analysis; the cases analysed here are therefore restricted to children whose Class A detections fell entirely within the six-virus panel. We restricted the present analysis to the six respiratory viruses (HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, IFV, covering both influenza A and B, and HMPV) flagged at the highest pathogenicity grade (Class A), for three reasons. First, these six viruses are the pathogens for which pathogen-specific climatic drivers are most biologically plausible and best characterized, allowing direct comparison with prior lagged-climate studies (Baker et al., 2019; Li et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2021). Second, restricting to Class A calls minimizes the inclusion of low-confidence or incidental detections. Third, bacterial and atypical pathogens are subject to different detection biases (for example, antibiotic pretreatment and colonization) and different climate–transmission mechanisms, and were therefore outside the scope of this analysis. Co-infections, defined as concurrent Class A detection of two or more of the six target viruses in the same specimen, were identified and are described in Section 2.4.2.3Meteorological dataMonthly city-wide meteorological summaries for Tianjin from January 2023 to December 2025 (n = 36 months) were obtained from the Tianjin Meteorological Bureau and comprised mean atmospheric pressure (hPa), mean wind speed (m/s), mean air temperature (°C), mean relative humidity (%), precipitation (mm) and mean daily sunshine duration (hours). Routine quality assurance included unit verification and column-order auditing across reporting periods. The meteorological series was time-aligned with the monthly aggregated viral case counts before analysis.We used monthly rather than daily or weekly data because the records available from the Tianjin Meteorological Bureau for this study period were supplied at monthly resolution; daily or weekly city-wide summaries were not accessible for the full 2023–2025 window. Finer (for example, weekly) resolution would allow more precise estimation of short-lag effects and is standard in DLNM-based climate–infection studies (Gasparrini et al., 2010; Li et al., 2025); we discuss this resolution constraint further in Section 4.6.2.4Statistical analysisCategorical data are presented as counts (percentages) and compared between groups with Pearson’s χ2 test; the assumption of an equal sex ratio was tested with the exact binomial test, and inter-pathogen age differences with the Kruskal–Wallis test. Daily case records were aggregated to monthly totals and merged with the meteorological time series. Yates’ continuity correction was applied to 2 × 2 comparisons.Co-infections were tabulated separately from the mono-infection pathogen spectrum. The primary pathogen-spectrum analysis (case counts, proportions, and demographic and specimen-type distributions in Section 3.1) attributes each specimen to a single, mutually exclusive pathogen row, so the per-pathogen counts in Table 1 sum to the total of 2,597 virus-positive cases; co-infection structure itself (pairwise combinations, and multiplicity) is tabulated separately, with each co-infected specimen contributing to every virus it carried, and is described in Section 3.4.Table 1Demographic and specimen characteristics of pediatric viral LRTI cases by pathogen.PathogenN (% of all positive)Male, n (%)Female, n (%)Sex p-valueAge, median (IQR), yLower respiratory tract specimen, n (%)HRV796 (30.7)471 (59.2)325 (40.8)<0.0014.0 (2.0–6.0)660 (82.9)ADV692 (26.6)425 (61.4)267 (38.6)<0.0016.0 (3.0–8.0)485 (70.1)RSV536 (20.6)304 (56.7)232 (43.3)0.0023.0 (1.0–4.0)454 (84.7)HBoV313 (12.1)179 (57.2)134 (42.8)0.0132.0 (1.0–4.0)277 (88.5)IFV155 (6.0)83 (53.5)72 (46.5)0.425.0 (2.0–7.0)123 (79.4)HMPV105 (4.0)66 (62.9)39 (37.1)0.0114.0 (1.8–6.0)74 (70.5)Pathogen counts are mutually exclusive per specimen (see Section 2.4), so the column totals sum to 2,597. Co-infected specimens, in which two or more Class A viruses were detected concurrently, are tabulated separately in Section 3.4, where each such specimen contributes to the count of every virus it carried; those pairwise counts are not reflected in the totals above. Sex p-values are from the exact binomial test against a 50:50 null; age is median (IQR) in years; Lower respiratory tract specimen = sputum or BALF.Pathogen–climate co-variation was screened with Spearman’s rank correlation (ρ) on the full monthly series and re-examined within meteorological seasons (spring, March–May; summer, June–August; autumn, September–November; winter, December–February).Lagged meteorological effects were examined in two complementary ways. First, cross-correlation functions were computed over lags of 0–6 months for temperature, relative humidity and wind speed. Second, lag-specific relative risks (RR) were derived from quasi-Poisson GLMs with a log link (Bhaskaran et al., 2013; Gasparrini, 2011; Imai et al., 2015) of the form log(μt) = α + β × Xt−L, where μt is the expected monthly case count in month t and Xt−L the meteorological exposure shifted back by L months (L = 0, 1, ..., 6). Because this analysis spans 126 model fits (6 pathogens × 3 variables × 7 lags), no formal correction for multiple comparisons was applied; signals reaching p<0.01 (for example, RSV with wind speed at a 1-month lag) are interpreted as relatively robust, whereas signals in the 0.01 to 0.05 range (for example, HMPV with temperature, and RSV with temperature) are flagged as exploratory. RR values are reported per clinically interpretable unit (5 °C for temperature, 10% for relative humidity and 0.5 m/s for wind speed), each chosen to approximate the interquartile span of the corresponding variable. Standard errors were corrected for overdispersion (Pearson dispersion parameter φ ≥ 1). For every pathogen × exposure combination, the lag at which the absolute log-RR was largest among significant lags is reported as the peak RR; the resulting post-hoc selection across candidate lags is discussed as a source of potential effect-size inflation in Section 4.6.This graded reading is a descriptive convention and does not control the family-wise error rate. Under the null hypothesis, roughly six of the 126 fits would be expected to reach p<0.05 by chance, and a Bonferroni-corrected threshold would fall at p<0.0004. We report uncorrected p-values on the reasoning that the six pathogens address distinct epidemiological questions rather than a single universal null, an approach with precedent in exploratory analyses of this kind (Rothman, 1990); the accompanying Type I error risk is set out explicitly in Section 4.6. Two associations in the 0.01 to 0.05 range are nonetheless carried into the Discussion, RSV with temperature and HMPV with temperature, and both are presented there as provisional, the HMPV signal explicitly as hypothesis-generating; no clinical or public health recommendation in this paper rests on either of them alone.Because the peak RR is the largest of up to seven correlated estimates, it is biased away from the null and its confidence interval is narrower than the selection process warrants, a general property of effect estimates identified by crossing a significance threshold in underpowered analyses (Ioannidis, 2008). full_text_sections.abstract: BackgroundFollowing the lifting of pandemic-era restrictions, China experienced a sharp resurgence in pediatric respiratory infections; however, post-pandemic epidemiological and climatic data on lower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs) from the temperate continental climate of northern China remain scarce.MethodsIn this retrospective, single-center surveillance study, we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of six respiratory viruses in children hospitalized with LRTI in Tianjin and assessed their pathogen-specific, lagged climatic associations. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). Pathogen–climate associations were estimated using a quasi-Poisson model that adjusted for seasonality, secular trend, and lagged meteorological exposures.ResultsAmong 2,597 virus-positive cases, the leading pathogens were HRV (30.7%), ADV (26.6%), and RSV (20.6%), followed by HBoV (12.1%), IFV (6.0%), and HMPV (4.0%). Age distributions differed by pathogen (p<0.05): RSV and HBoV predominated in infants and toddlers, HRV and HMPV in preschoolers, ADV in school-aged children, and IFV across the older preschool-to-school-age range; males predominated for all viruses except IFV. Five viruses peaked in December, whereas HBoV peaked uniquely in July. After adjustment for seasonality and secular trend, the unadjusted associations of IFV with humidity and temperature disappeared, indicating that they largely reflected shared seasonality. In contrast, RSV retained associations with temperature (RR 3.87, 95% CI 1.39–10.76) and wind speed (RR 5.46, 95% CI 2.39–12.47) at a 1-month lag, and HMPV with temperature (RR 13.3, 95% CI 1.64–108.3; imprecise given its low case count); HRV, ADV, and HBoV showed no independent climatic associations. Co-infections occurred in 116 cases (4.5%), most frequently HBoV+HRV (23.3%).ConclusionPost-pandemic pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin shows distinctive pathogen-specific profiles in age, seasonality, and climatic sensitivity. The summer peak of HBoV and the seasonally independent climatic drivers of RSV and HMPV provide a preliminary basis that, if confirmed with higher-resolution data, could inform pathogen-tailored, climate-informed surveillance in northern Chinese megacities.
full_text_sections.methods: 2Materials and methods2.1Study design, setting and populationWe conducted a retrospective single-center surveillance study at the Department of Respiratory Medicine, Tianjin Children’s Hospital (Ma-Chang campus), the only tertiary-A comprehensive children’s hospital in Tianjin. The hospital is the principal pediatric referral center for Tianjin municipality and, for selected specialties, draws patients from across the wider North China Plain; publicly reported hospital-wide figures indicate roughly 17,000–20,000 pediatric admissions per year across all departments. Our cohort of 2,597 virologically confirmed viral LRTI cases represents the subset of hospitalized LRTI cases that were both tested and found positive for one of the six target viruses, not the total burden of pediatric LRTI hospitalization in Tianjin. A precise, denominator-based estimate of the proportion of all Tianjin pediatric LRTI hospitalizations captured by this cohort is not available, because no citywide pediatric LRTI hospitalization registry exists for comparison. As a tertiary referral center, the cohort is likely enriched for more severe disease and for cases referred from primary and secondary facilities; this referral pattern, and the resulting limit on generalizability to primary care, is revisited in the Discussion (Section 4.6).Eligible participants were children aged 0–18 years hospitalized with a clinical diagnosis of LRTI between 1 January 2023 and 31 December 2025, from whom a respiratory specimen was submitted for routine viral testing. LRTI was defined clinically, following the 2019 Chinese Pediatric Society guideline for community-acquired pneumonia (Subspecialty Group of Respiratory Diseases, 2019), as cough or fever (axillary temperature ≥38 °C) together with at least one of: tachypnoea, wheezing, crackles on auscultation, or imaging evidence of pneumonia or bronchiolitis. This definition captures the clinical syndromes of pneumonia and bronchiolitis and excludes isolated upper respiratory tract infection. We excluded children with pre-existing chronic respiratory disease, congenital airway malformations, documented immunodeficiency, active malignancy, or concurrent infection by pathogens outside the predefined six-virus panel. This last criterion operated at the level of the child rather than of the laboratory result: whenever the tNGS report carried a Class A detection of a bacterial, atypical or non-panel viral pathogen alongside one of the six target viruses, the case was removed from the cohort at eligibility screening, so no such child contributes to any analysis reported here. For viruses prone to subclinical carriage, chiefly HRV and HBoV, a detection was considered clinically causative only when the tNGS reporting algorithm assigned a pathogenicity Class A grade, the clinical picture matched the corresponding viral syndrome, and other plausible infectious causes had been clinically excluded (residual misclassification risk for these two viruses is discussed in Section 4.6). For descriptive analyses, children were stratified a priori into four age categories: infants (<1 year), toddlers (1–2 years), preschoolers (3–5 years) and school-aged children (≥6 years). All records were de-identified before analysis. The study followed the Declaration of Helsinki and was approved by the Institutional Ethics Committee of Tianjin Children’s Hospital (approval number 2024-LXKY-023); written informed consent was waived given the retrospective design and full de-identification of the dataset.2.2Pathogen detectionRespiratory specimens (sputum, the predominant type; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF; nasopharyngeal swabs; and oropharyngeal swabs) were collected following standardized clinical protocols, placed into viral transport medium, and transported within two hours at 2–8 °C to the clinical laboratory. Total nucleic acids were extracted on an automated platform following the manufacturer’s instructions. All specimens were tested with the same commercial targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) panel, which simultaneously screens for respiratory bacteria, viruses, atypical pathogens and antimicrobial-resistance markers. Library construction, ultra-multiplex amplification of pathogen-specific genomic regions and Illumina-compatible high-throughput sequencing were performed following the manufacturer’s recommended workflow, with reads aligned against a curated pathogen reference database (Li et al., 2025; Shang et al., 2025). The vendor’s reporting algorithm assigned each detected organism a clinical pathogenicity grade, from Class A (highest confidence) through lower-confidence grades. The panel was introduced during 2023 and reached full clinical implementation in the fourth quarter of that year, after which testing volume remained broadly stable through 2024 and 2025. Monthly counts of tNGS requests could not be retrieved from the laboratory information system for the whole study window, so this account of testing volume rests on the laboratory’s implementation record rather than on an auditable series of test counts, and it should be read as such.The grade is a composite call rather than a single read-count cut-off. It is generated by an integrated scoring system that combines normalized read counts (reads per million, RPM), the breadth of genome coverage achieved across the targeted regions, and species-level annotation of pathogenicity against a curated reference database; Class A is assigned to organisms that meet the pre-specified RPM and coverage criteria for a clinically significant pathogen. The numerical RPM and coverage cut-offs behind the grade are proprietary to the assay vendor and are not released to the ordering laboratory; we are therefore unable to report them, and the grade as issued was the only form in which this information was available to us. Grading was prospective in the sense that it was performed by the clinical laboratory at the time the routine diagnostic report was issued and used for patient care, and the research team did not re-adjudicate the classifications retrospectively. No Class A detection was subsequently excluded on the grounds of clinical mismatch, because the Class A flag served as an inclusion criterion for the six-virus panel rather than as the sole determinant of clinical causality; for HRV and HBoV, the additional clinical adjudication described in Section 2.1 was applied instead.The full panel detects a broader range of organisms than the six viruses analyzed here. Common bacterial pathogens reported by the full panel include Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Moraxella catarrhalis and Staphylococcus aureus; the atypical pathogens include Mycoplasma pneumoniae and Chlamydia pneumoniae; and respiratory viruses outside the six-virus panel, including parainfluenza viruses, seasonal coronaviruses and SARS-CoV-2, are likewise covered. Consistent with the eligibility criteria set out in Section 2.1, a child in whom any of these organisms was reported concurrently with one of the six target viruses was excluded from the cohort at screening rather than merely omitted from the analysis; the cases analysed here are therefore restricted to children whose Class A detections fell entirely within the six-virus panel. We restricted the present analysis to the six respiratory viruses (HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, IFV, covering both influenza A and B, and HMPV) flagged at the highest pathogenicity grade (Class A), for three reasons. First, these six viruses are the pathogens for which pathogen-specific climatic drivers are most biologically plausible and best characterized, allowing direct comparison with prior lagged-climate studies (Baker et al., 2019; Li et al., 2025; Xu et al., 2021). Second, restricting to Class A calls minimizes the inclusion of low-confidence or incidental detections. full_text_sections.results: 3Results3.1Overall pathogen distribution and demographicsAcross 36 surveillance months we identified 2,597 virologically confirmed pediatric LRTI cases. HRV was the most frequently detected virus (796 cases, 30.7%), followed by ADV (692, 26.6%), RSV (536, 20.6%), HBoV (313, 12.1%), IFV (155, 6.0%) and HMPV (105, 4.0%) (Figure 2A; Table 1). Sputum was the predominant specimen type for HRV, RSV, HBoV, HMPV and IFV. The proportion of cases sampled from the lower airway (sputum or BALF) likewise differed across pathogens (χ2 = 73.7, df = 5, p < 0.001), ranging from 70.1% for ADV and 70.5% for HMPV to 88.5% for HBoV (Table 1). ADV was more evenly distributed across specimen types, with BALF (35.4%) and sputum (34.7%) contributing similar shares and nasopharyngeal swabs a further 29.6%, giving ADV a markedly higher BALF share than the other five viruses (Figure 2B). Annual case counts rose from 188 in 2023 to 1,027 in 2024 and 1,382 in 2025 (Figure 2C). The 2023 figures warrant particular caution on this account. The assay reached full clinical implementation only in the fourth quarter of that year (Section 2.2), so the 188 cases recorded in 2023 almost certainly under-represent circulation during the early post-pandemic period relative to 2024 and 2025, when testing volume was broadly stable. Subsequent analyses therefore emphasize pathogen composition, age distribution and seasonal timing, which are far less sensitive to testing volume than absolute case counts.Figure 2Overall pathogen spectrum and specimen characteristics of pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin, 2023–2025. (A) Case distribution across the six viral pathogens, ranked by prevalence. (B) Specimen-type composition by pathogen. (C) Annual case burden, stacked by pathogen.Grouped bar and stacked bar chart panel showing (A) case numbers and percentages for six pathogens, (B) specimen composition by pathogen, and (C) annual case burden from 2023 to 2025. HRV and ADV have the highest positive cases, sputum is the most common specimen, and total case burden increases each year, with pathogen contribution shown by color.Two features of the assay bound the influence of testing volume without removing it. All six viruses sit on a single multiplex panel and are screened simultaneously in every specimen, so no virus could be tested more often than another, and a change in ordering volume alters which children were tested rather than which viruses were sought. What this cannot exclude is a shift in case mix: if tNGS was ordered preferentially for more severely ill children, and if the pathogen spectrum of severe admissions differs from that of milder ones, composition will move with ordering practice. The markedly higher BALF share of ADV (Figure 2B) is consistent with such a gradient, and the point is developed in Section 4.6.Boys predominated for HRV (59.2%, p<0.001), ADV (61.4%, p<0.001), RSV (56.7%, p=0.002), HBoV (57.2%, p=0.013) and HMPV (62.9%, p=0.011), whereas IFV showed a balanced sex ratio (53.5% male, p=0.42) (Table 1; Figure 3A). Although IFV was the only virus without a male excess, a χ2 test for heterogeneity across the six pathogens did not reach significance (χ2 = 5.77, df = 5, p = 0.33), and neither did the comparison of IFV against the other five viruses combined (χ2 = 1.68, df = 1, p = 0.20). The balanced ratio for IFV is therefore better read as a failure to demonstrate a male excess in the smallest of the larger groups (n = 155) than as evidence of a genuinely different sex distribution.Figure 3Demographic composition of pediatric viral LRTI by pathogen. (A) Sex distribution, with binomial-test significance markers. (B) Age (years) by pathogen (median, IQR), with jittered individual data points overlaid. Significance markers: *p<0.05, **p<0.01, ***p<0.001; ns = not significant.Bar chart on the left shows male and female sex distribution for six pathogens with males consistently higher for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, and HMPV; differences denoted by statistical significance symbols. Boxplot on the right displays age distribution in years for each pathogen with medians, interquartile ranges, and data points, indicating variation in median ages by pathogen.Age distributions differed sharply across pathogens (Kruskal–Wallis H = 372.7, p < 0.001; Figure 3B). Infants and toddlers carried most HBoV (median 2.0 [IQR 1.0–4.0] years) and RSV (3.0 [1.0–4.0]) cases; preschoolers were the main group for HRV (4.0 [2.0–6.0]) and HMPV (4.0 [1.8–6.0]); ADV predominated in school-aged children (6.0 [3.0–8.0]), while IFV spanned the older preschool-to-school-age range (median 5.0 [2.0–7.0]) (Table 1; Figure 3B).3.2Temporal distributionMonthly time-series of the six pathogens (Figure 4A) showed strong but pathogen-specific seasonality. HRV, ADV, RSV, IFV and HMPV all reached their annual maxima in December, consistent with the cold, dry continental winter being the dominant transmission season in northern China. The December peak of late 2024 (about 400 positive cases that month) was the largest monthly count of the surveillance period, with a smaller but still notable winter peak in December 2025. HBoV behaved differently, showing a single summer maximum in July. ADV showed a secondary peak in late spring (April–May), and HRV and ADV together produced the broadest seasonal envelope (March–December) of any pathogen. The seasonal heatmap (Figure 4B) summarizes these patterns: each virus shows at least one clearly defined month-of-year peak, and HBoV is the only virus to peak in a warm-season month (July). Because the heatmap is normalized row-wise, color intensity for each pathogen is scaled to its own monthly range; the visual prominence of a peak for a low-incidence pathogen (for example, HMPV) therefore does not indicate the same absolute case count as for a high-incidence pathogen (for example, HRV).Figure 4Temporal distribution of pediatric viral LRTI, 2023–2025. (A) Stacked monthly case counts by pathogen. (B) Seasonal heatmap of mean monthly cases by pathogen; cell shading is normalized row-wise so that each pathogen’s twelve-month profile can be read on a comparable scale.Stacked bar chart and heatmap visualizing monthly viral pathogen detections from January 2023 to December 2025. The chart (panel A) shows case counts for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV, IFV, and HMPV, with peaks observed between late 2024 and early 2025. The heatmap (panel B) presents mean cases per month for each virus, highlighting increased relative intensity for most pathogens in November and December, with values labeled within cells and a scale indicating intensity from low (yellow) to high (red).3.3Seasonal and meteorological analyses3.3.1Overall pathogen–climate correlationsOverall Spearman rank correlations (Figure 5A; Table 2) showed a significant positive correlation between HBoV and temperature (ρ = +0.34, p = 0.04). ADV (ρ = +0.32, p = 0.06), HRV (ρ = +0.28, p = 0.10) and RSV (ρ = +0.24, p = 0.16) showed positive but non-significant trends. IFV and HMPV showed non-significant negative correlations with temperature (ρ = −0.27 and −0.05). Relative humidity followed a similar pattern: HBoV (+0.33), ADV (+0.30) and HRV (+0.28) correlated positively, whereas IFV (−0.29) and HMPV (−0.23) correlated negatively. Wind speed produced predominantly negative correlations across the six viruses, strongest for HBoV (−0.32), ADV (−0.30) and HRV (−0.29).Figure 5Pathogen–meteorology correlations. (B) Seasonal distribution of temperature, relative humidity and wind speed. (C–F) Season-stratified Spearman ρ for the three core exposures across spring, summer, autumn and winter, using the same −1 to +1 symmetric scale. full_text_sections.discussion: 4DiscussionIn this three-year, single-center cohort we characterized the post-pandemic epidemiology of pediatric viral LRTI in Tianjin, a megacity on the North China Plain, and quantified how closely monthly viral activity tracks ambient weather. To our knowledge, the dataset is unusual for northern China in spanning six respiratory viruses, including the comparatively under-surveyed HRV, HBoV and HMPV, over the full 2023–2025 post-pandemic rebound window, with a complete and time-matched monthly meteorological record.4.1Principal epidemiological featuresAcross the six viruses, HRV, ADV and RSV were the leading causes of pediatric LRTI, and each pathogen carried a well-defined demographic profile. Age and sex stratification confirmed recognized biological gradients. RSV and HBoV were most prevalent in infants and toddlers, in line with airway and immune development (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Li et al., 2022); ADV peaked in school-aged children and IFV in the older preschool-to-school-age range, consistent with close-contact transmission in schools and other crowded settings (Fang et al., 2025; Yu et al., 2021; Zhang et al., 2023); and HMPV showed an intermediate distribution. The older age skew of IFV fits its epidemiology in temperate regions, where school-aged children are the principal drivers of seasonal influenza transmission and the group in which symptomatic infection is most readily recognized, in contrast to the infant and toddler predominance of RSV and HBoV (Feng et al., 2024; Klein and Flanagan, 2016). The male predominance for HRV, ADV, RSV, HBoV and HMPV, but not IFV, echoes prior pediatric LRTI cohorts and may reflect sex differences in innate immunity and behavior (Klein and Flanagan, 2016). The strong age-group × pathogen association reinforces the need for an explicitly age-stratified surveillance framework.The six pathogens also fell into two distinct seasonal groups. HRV, ADV, RSV, IFV and HMPV all peaked in December, during the cold, dry continental winter, whereas HBoV stood apart with an isolated July maximum—the only warm-season peak of the panel. HRV additionally displayed the broadest seasonal envelope, circulating from March to December, consistent with fundamentally endemic, weakly seasonal behavior. Because the rise in absolute case counts partly reflects expanding testing volume rather than incidence (Section 3.1), the interpretation that follows rests on pathogen composition, age structure and seasonal timing rather than on raw counts.4.2Interpretation in the post-pandemic contextThese patterns are best read against, rather than directly measured against, pre-pandemic Chinese pediatric surveillance, since our cohort describes the post-pandemic period without a matched pre-pandemic Tianjin comparator. Several multi-center Chinese studies contrasting pre-pandemic (2018–2019) with post-pandemic (2023 onward) cohorts have reported a broadly consistent post-pandemic pattern: higher overall pathogen positivity and mixed-infection rates, a higher proportion of severe presentations, and shifts in the relative ranking, seasonal timing and age distribution of individual pathogens (Cui et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025). In Shanghai, post-pandemic test positivity rose markedly relative to 2019, with both RSV and ADV increasing and RSV’s onset shifting earlier into August, ahead of its conventional winter season (Liu et al., 2025); other Chinese cohorts spanning the pre-pandemic, pandemic and post-pandemic phases have likewise documented altered seasonal timing and age-distribution shifts for RSV, ADV and rhinovirus after non-pharmaceutical interventions were relaxed (Cui et al., 2024).Interpreted against this backdrop, our Tianjin observations show both continuities and departures. HRV’s endemic, weakly seasonal circulation—reflected in its leading position and broad March–December envelope—appears to have been less perturbed by the pandemic and its aftermath than that of the more strongly seasonal viruses. By contrast, the convergence of five of the six viruses onto a single sharp December peak is consistent with the compressed, intensified post-pandemic winter surge described elsewhere in China, plausibly reflecting the accumulated immunity debt from population-level exposure gaps in 2020–2022 (Cohen et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024) superimposed on the resumption of normal contact patterns. HBoV departed most sharply from this winter pattern, peaking instead in summer; to our knowledge, such an isolated warm-season peak has not been prominently reported as a post-pandemic phenomenon elsewhere in China. Whether it reflects a genuine post-pandemic shift in HBoV’s seasonal niche or a feature specific to Tianjin’s continental climate cannot be resolved with a single-center, single-period dataset, and we return to its biological and clinical significance in Section 4.4.4.3Climate-driven lagged effectsThe unadjusted and seasonally adjusted analyses answer different questions, and reading them together guards against a common pitfall in climate–infection studies. In the unadjusted analysis (Table 3), IFV appeared the most climate-responsive virus, with antecedent humidity and temperature aligning with later case counts, in keeping with the recognized seasonal phasing of influenza in temperate climates (Deyle et al., 2016; Kudo et al., 2019; Lowen et al., 2007; Lowen and Steel, 2014). Once seasonality and secular trend were held constant in the unified model, however, these IFV associations disappeared (Table 5). This does not mean that IFV has no climatic drivers. Rather, because ambient temperature and humidity in Tianjin themselves follow an almost perfect annual sinusoid, they are nearly collinear with the sine–cosine seasonal terms of the unified model; for a virus as tightly locked to the annual cycle as influenza (77.5% of deviance explained by season and trend alone), the model simply cannot separate the effect of “season” from that of “temperature” or “humidity.” The most that can be concluded is that, at the present monthly resolution, IFV shows no climatic association detectable independently of the seasonal cycle itself.The seasonally adjusted model instead isolated RSV and HMPV as the only viruses with climate associations independent of shared seasonality (Table 5): RSV tracked temperature and wind speed at short lags, while HMPV tracked temperature positively and humidity inversely, although its low case counts make these estimates imprecise and hypothesis-generating. HRV, ADV and HBoV showed no independent lagged signal, indicating that at monthly resolution their seasonal envelopes are not accompanied by a detectable climate effect beyond the annual cycle. This null result should not be read as evidence of climatic insensitivity. For these three viruses the seasonal-plus-trend baseline itself explained comparatively little of the monthly deviance (HRV 41.5%, HBoV 28.6%, ADV 17.1%; Table 4), so a large share of the variation in their case counts is left unaccounted for by season, trend and weather combined. Residual variation of that magnitude widens the standard errors, and with 36 monthly observations spanning three seasonal cycles only associations of substantial size could reach significance. A modest but real climate effect would probably have escaped detection here, and the finding is better described as uninformative for HRV, ADV and HBoV than as negative. The contrast between the two analyses carries the key methodological lesson: lagged climate associations in surveillance data can be interpreted only after seasonality has been accounted for.These post-pandemic patterns can be read against the pre-pandemic national baseline of Xu et al. (2021), who modelled a seven-virus panel—five of them shared with our own—across 81 sentinel hospitals in 22 Chinese provinces (2009–2013) and ranked the meteorological factors by climate region. For the temperate north, to which Tianjin belongs, three points agree wit…
full_text_sections.conclusion: 5ConclusionAcross 36 months of post-pandemic surveillance in Tianjin (2,597 confirmed cases), HRV, ADV and RSV were the leading viral causes of pediatric LRTI, and each of the six viruses carried a distinctive age, sex, seasonal and specimen-type profile. In a unified model adjusting simultaneously for seasonality and secular trend, RSV and HMPV, rather than IFV, showed the clearest evidence of an independent, non-seasonal climate association, whereas IFV’s prominent unadjusted climate signal proved to reflect its strong intrinsic seasonality. HBoV showed a singular July epidemic at odds with the December convergence of the other viruses, together providing a preliminary basis for pathogen-tailored early warning and prevention in northern Chinese megacities. Co-infection occurred in 4.5% of positives, centered on HRV-containing combinations whose clinical severity remains to be defined. Set alongside pre-pandemic Chinese pediatric surveillance, these findings are broadly consistent with a post-pandemic pattern of intensified, temporally compressed winter transmission, while HBoV’s summer epidemic appears to be a locally distinctive feature warranting further study. If confirmed with higher-resolution, denominator-based data, these findings could inform a hospital-level operational calendar anchored on the December peak and the secondary July HBoV peak, climate-informed early warning tailored to each pathogen’s actual (seasonally adjusted) climate sensitivity, and a refined strategy for vaccination, RSV passive immunization and infection control. Such confirmation will require multi-center cohorts, denominator-based positivity metrics, weekly- or daily-resolution meteorology, and direct pre- versus post-pandemic comparison.
full_text_sections.other: 1IntroductionLower respiratory tract infections (LRTIs)—comprising pneumonia, bronchiolitis, and related lower-airway syndromes—remain leading causes of pediatric hospitalization and mortality in children under five worldwide, with viruses accounting for the overwhelming majority of cases (Nair et al., 2010; Mulholland, 2003; Li et al., 2022). In contrast to generally self-limiting upper respiratory infections, viral LRTIs account disproportionately for admissions requiring supplemental oxygen and intensive care; moreover, certain pathogens, notably RSV and HRV, are implicated in long-term sequelae including recurrent wheeze and asthma (Li et al., 2022; Bizot et al., 2021; Royston and Tapparel, 2016). In China, the burden is amplified by dense urban populations, overlapping pathogen circulation, and the high contact rates among school-aged children, all of which sustain substantial LRTI-related hospitalizations (Cui et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025). Following the lifting of pandemic-era non-pharmaceutical interventions, several Chinese regions reported atypical, out-of-season resurgences of RSV, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and ADV (Del Riccio et al., 2024; Liu et al., 2025). These have been attributed both to an immunity gap accumulated during 2020–2022 and to the re-establishment of pre-pandemic transmission networks (Cohen et al., 2021; Li et al., 2024). Despite this evolving landscape, most national surveillance efforts remain narrowly focused on classical pathogens (RSV, ADV, IFV) or aggregate all respiratory infections irrespective of anatomical site. Consequently, the post-pandemic, multi-pathogen epidemiology of viral LRTI specifically in children—particularly at the city level, where targeted surveillance is most actionable—remains inadequately characterized (Terliesner et al., 2022; Xia et al., 2026).Ambient weather conditions are well-established modulators of respiratory virus transmission, operating through both physical and host-defense mechanisms (Baker et al., 2019; Xu et al., 2021). Cold, dry air favors the persistence and airborne dispersal of enveloped viruses such as RSV and influenza by stabilizing the lipid envelope, slowing droplet evaporation, and impairing upper-airway mucociliary clearance (Kudo et al., 2019; Lowen et al., 2007; Lowen and Steel, 2014). Non-enveloped viruses, including ADV and HBoV, whose protein capsids tolerate a wider range of environmental stressors, tend to circulate more evenly throughout the year (Chen et al., 2014b; Lion, 2014). Importantly, climate–virus relationships are non-linear and time-delayed; exposures occurring days to weeks before case surges often exert the dominant effect, a structure that makes distributed lag non-linear models (DLNMs) particularly suitable for fine-grained inference (Bhaskaran et al., 2013; Gasparrini et al., 2010; Gasparrini, 2011). A recent post-pandemic study from Wuhan, in central China, applied daily-resolution DLNMs to seven respiratory pathogens and identified distinct lagged climate patterns—most notably, humidity drops as 1–2-week antecedents of RSV surges and wind speed as a leading correlate of influenza activity (Li et al., 2025). Because only monthly-resolution meteorological data were available for the present 2023–2025 window (Section 2.3), a full DLNM cross-basis was not identifiable with the available degrees of freedom; we therefore adapted the same distributed-lag logic into a screening framework of single-lag quasi-Poisson models spanning 0–6-month lags, cross-validated against cross-correlation functions and, in a second step, adjusted for seasonality and secular trend within a unified model (Section 2.4). This approach is best viewed as a monthly-resolution approximation to the DLNM framework rather than a full non-linear cross-basis estimation.However, few studies have systematically examined this multi-pathogen landscape in northern China, where the continental monsoon climate—characterized by cold, dry winters; hot, humid summers; and pronounced seasonal swings in temperature, humidity, and wind—differs markedly from the subtropical conditions of Wuhan and other southern cities (Chen et al., 2014a; Cui et al., 2015; Yin et al., 2023). Tianjin, a megacity of 13 million on the North China Plain, offers a particularly valuable setting to address this gap. Its local viral spectrum extends beyond the four classical agents to include three pathogens that are less consistently surveilled but contribute substantially to pediatric LRTI: HRV, HBoV, and HMPV (Feng et al., 2024; Jiang et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2022; Zhu et al., 2020). Prior work in this area has concentrated largely on southern China or on the classical pathogens (RSV, ADV, IFV), and the lagged climatic effects of the less consistently surveilled HRV, HBoV and HMPV under a temperate continental climate have not been systematically evaluated. Precisely how these three viruses, alongside the classical agents, track climatic exposures across different lag intervals in northern China therefore remains poorly characterized—a knowledge gap that has direct implications for the design of climate-informed early-warning systems in the region.To address this, we analyzed three years of post-pandemic surveillance data (January 2023 to December 2025) from a tertiary children’s hospital in Tianjin, encompassing 2,597 virologically confirmed pediatric LRTI cases caused by six respiratory viruses. Our objectives were: (i) to describe the demographic, temporal, and specimen-type distributions of each pathogen; (ii) to characterize co-infection patterns; (iii) to test pathogen-specific associations with monthly meteorological variables using Spearman correlation and season-stratified analyses; and (iv) to evaluate lagged climate effects across 0- to 6-month intervals using cross-correlation functions and a unified quasi-Poisson generalized linear model that simultaneously adjusts for seasonality and secular trends. Finally, we discuss the practical implications of our findings for climate-informed early-warning systems and pathogen-tailored preventive strategies in northern Chinese megacities. 2.2Pathogen detectionRespiratory specimens (sputum, the predominant type; bronchoalveolar lavage fluid, BALF; nasopharyngeal swabs; and oropharyngeal swabs) were collected following standardized clinical protocols, placed into viral transport medium, and transported within two hours at 2–8 °C to the clinical laboratory. Total nucleic acids were extracted on an automated platform following the manufacturer’s instructions. All specimens were tested with the same commercial targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) panel, which simultaneously screens for respiratory bacteria, viruses, atypical pathogens and antimicrobial-resistance markers. Library construction, ultra-multiplex amplification of pathogen-specific genomic regions and Illumina-compatible high-throughput sequencing were performed following the manufacturer’s recommended workflow, with reads aligned against a curated pathogen reference database (Li et al., 2025; Shang et al., 2025). The vendor’s reporting algorithm assigned each detected organism a clinical pathogenicity grade, from Class A (highest confidence) through lower-confidence grades. The panel was introduced during 2023 and reached full clinical implementation in the fourth quarter of that year, after which testing volume remained broadly stable through 2024 and 2025. elements_zh.methods: 使用准泊松模型估计病原体与气候的关联,该模型考虑了季节性、长期趋势和滞后气象暴露因素。结果:在2,597例病毒阳性病例中,主要病原体为HRV(30.7%)、ADV(26.6%)和RSV(20.6%),随后是HBoV(12.1%)、IFV(6.0%)和HMPV(4.0%)。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV和HBoV在婴儿和幼儿中最为常见,这与气道和免疫系统发育一致(Feng等,2024;Jiang等,2016;Li等,2022);ADV在学龄儿童中达到高峰,IFV在较大的学龄前至学龄儿童群体中达到高峰,这与学校及其他拥挤环境中的密切接触有关(Fang等,2025;Yu等,2021;Zhang等,2023);而HMPV则表现出中间分布。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 据我们所知,该数据集在北方中国较为罕见,因为它涵盖了2023–2025年疫情后反弹期间的六种呼吸道病毒,包括相对较少被调查的HRV、HBoV和HMPV,并且具有完整且时间匹配的每月气象记录。4.1主要流行病学特征:在六种病毒中,HRV、ADV和RSV是导致儿童下呼吸道感染的主要原因,每种病原体都有明确的流行病学特征。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 强年龄组 × 病原体关联进一步强调了需要一个明确的年龄分层监测框架。这六种病原体也分为两个不同的季节性群体。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在阳性病例中有4.5%发生了共感染,主要集中在包含HRV的组合中,其临床严重程度仍需进一步定义。

analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: To our knowledge, the dataset is unusual for northern China in spanning six respiratory viruses, including the comparatively under-surveyed HRV, HBoV and HMPV, over the full 2023–2025 post-pandemic rebound window, with a complete and time-matched monthly meteorological record.4.1Principal epidemiological featuresAcross the six viruses, HRV, ADV and RSV were the leading causes of pediatric LRTI, and each pathogen carried a well-defined demographic profile.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The strong age-group × pathogen association reinforces the need for an explicitly age-stratified surveillance framework.The six pathogens also fell into two distinct seasonal groups.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Co-infection occurred in 4.5% of positives, centered on HRV-containing combinations whose clinical severity remains to be defined.

This last criterion operated at the level of the child rather than of the laboratory result: whenever the tNGS report carried a Class A detection of a bacterial, atypical or non-panel viral pathogen alongside one of the six target viruses, the case was removed from the cohort at eligibility screening, so no such child contributes to any analysis reported here. Children aged 0–18 years hospitalized between January 2023 and December 2025 were tested by targeted next-generation sequencing for human rhinovirus (HRV), adenovirus (ADV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human bocavirus (HBoV), influenza virus (IFV), and human metapneumovirus (HMPV). papers.abstract_zh: 背景:在解除疫情管控措施后,中国经历了儿童呼吸道感染的急剧回升;然而,关于来自中国北方大陆性气候地区的下呼吸道感染(LRTIs)的疫情后流行病学和气候数据仍然稀缺。方法:本研究是一项回顾性单中心监测研究,我们描述了2023–2025年疫情后天津市住院儿童中六种呼吸道病毒的流行病学,并评估了这些病毒的病原体特异性及滞后气候关联。2材料与方法2.1研究设计、设置和人群:我们在天津市儿童医院(马场校区)呼吸科开展了一项回顾性单中心监测研究,这是天津市唯一的三级甲等综合性儿童医院。这一标准适用于儿童而非实验室结果:每当tNGS报告中检测到细菌、非典型或非检测面板病毒病原体的同时也检测到六种目标病毒之一时,该病例将在资格筛选时被排除,因此没有这样的儿童参与本研究中报告的任何分析。2023年1月至2025年12月期间住院的0–18岁儿童接受了针对人类鼻病毒(HRV)、腺病毒(ADV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、人类博卡病毒(HBoV)、流感病毒(IFV)和人偏肺病毒(HMPV)的靶向下一代测序检测。使用准泊松模型估计病原体与气候的关联,该模型考虑了季节性、长期趋势和滞后气象暴露。结果:在2,597例病毒阳性病例中,主要病原体为HRV(30.7%)、ADV(26.6%)和RSV(20.6%),随后是HBoV(12.1%)、IFV(6.0%)和HMPV(4.0%)(图2A;表1)
papers.summary_zh: 背景:在解除疫情管控措施后,中国经历了儿童呼吸道感染的急剧回升;然而,关于来自中国北方大陆性气候地区的下呼吸道感染(LRTIs)的疫情后流行病学和气候数据仍然稀缺。方法:本研究是一项回顾性单中心监测研究,我们描述了2023–2025年疫情后天津市住院儿童中六种呼吸道病毒的流行病学,并评估了这些病毒的病原体特异性及滞后气候关联。2材料与方法2.1研究设计、设置和人群:我们在天津市儿童医院(马场校区)呼吸科开展了一项回顾性单中心监测研究,这是天津市唯一的三级甲等综合性儿童医院。这一标准适用于儿童而非实验室结果:每当tNGS报告中检测到细菌、非典型或非检测面板病毒病原体的同时也检测到六种目标病毒之一时,该病例将在资格筛选时被排除,因此没有这样的儿童参与本研究中报告的任何分析。2023年1月至2025年12月期间住院的0–18岁儿童接受了针对人类鼻病毒(HRV)、腺病毒(ADV)、呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)、人类博卡病毒(HBoV)、流感病毒(IFV)和人偏肺病毒(HMPV)的靶向下一代测序检测。使用准泊松模型估计病原体与气候的关联,该模型考虑了季节性、长期趋势和滞后气象暴露。结果:在2,597例病毒阳性病例中,主要病原体为HRV(30.7%)、ADV(26.6%)和RSV(20.6%),随后是HBoV(12.1%)、IFV(6.0%)和HMPV(4.0%)(图2A;表1)

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: (C) 按病原体分组的年度病例负担。分组条形图和堆叠条形图面板显示(A)六种病原体的病例数和百分比,(B)标本组成按病原体分组,以及(C)2023至2025年的年度病例负担。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用准泊松模型估计病原体与气候的关联,该模型考虑了季节性、长期趋势和滞后气象暴露因素。结果:在2,597例病毒阳性病例中,主要病原体为HRV(30.7%)、ADV(26.6%)和RSV(20.6%),随后是HBoV(12.1%)、IFV(6.0%)和HMPV(4.0%)。
analysis_zh.main_results: RSV和HBoV在婴儿和幼儿中最为常见,这与气道和免疫系统发育一致(Feng等,2024;Jiang等,2016;Li等,2022);ADV在学龄儿童中达到高峰,IFV在较大的学龄前至学龄儿童群体中达到高峰,这与学校及其他拥挤环境中的密切接触有关(Fang等,2025;Yu等,2021;Zhang等,2023);而HMPV则表现出中间分布。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 据我们所知,该数据集在北方中国较为罕见,因为它涵盖了2023–2025年疫情后反弹期间的六种呼吸道病毒,包括相对较少被调查的HRV、HBoV和HMPV,并且具有完整且时间匹配的每月气象记录。4.1主要流行病学特征:在六种病毒中,HRV、ADV和RSV是导致儿童下呼吸道感染的主要原因,每种病原体都有明确的流行病学特征。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 强年龄组 × 病原体关联进一步强调了需要一个明确的年龄分层监测框架。这六种病原体也分为两个不同的季节性群体。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 在阳性病例中有4.5%发生了共感染,主要集中在包含HRV的组合中,其临床严重程度仍需进一步定义。
